newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - IBM seen extended near-term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IBM seen extended near-term.

text.p: Shares in International Business Machines Corp flirted with their all-time closing high on Tuesday, but analysts said the stock may be close to topping out for the near term.
Technical analysts said that a recent wave of bullish sentiment toward IBM, viewed as a contrarian indicator, will likely work against further gains in the near future.

The likelihood Wall Street stocks will see some general near-term profit taking will also affect IBM, they said. But after pausing, the stock appears poised to drive over the $200 level on a pre-split basis, they added.
"This move (in IBM) is extended to the upside," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities.
IBM ended flat at 173-1/2 on Tuesday, nearing its all-time closing high of 175-7/8 set in August 1987. Earlier in the day it traded as high as 177-1/8.
The stock has surged from a recent low of 129-1/4 on April 4 on a series of bullish developments, including better-than- expected first quarter earnings, a increased dividend and a stock split.
The key breakout point for IBM came on Monday when it drove through the 170-1/8 level, which was its intra-day high hit January 21 before the stock retraced to its April low.
"It went through (170-1/8) like wet spaghetti," said Gary Kaltbaum, technical analyst at JW Charles.
Technical analysts said the saw near-term support on IBM's chart around the low-$160 area.
While IBM has gained momentum from the sharp rally in Wall Street over the past month, the stock will probably be affected by near-term profit-taking in the market as well, the analysts said.
"I believe the market is just simply getting overbought and we're going to have a natural dose of profit taking, which I think is also going to influence IBM," Nie said.
But after some consolidation, the stock is seen marching higher. "I think it could go into the $200s," Kaltbaum said. "It's got a real good chance, but it's got work to do."
